answer: Each agent must stake a bond that peers can slash the moment the same hardware registers a second persona. One honest joiner pays little; ten thousand duplicates become ruinous, so a sybil farm burns real capital before it casts a vote. Arrivals also need attestation through recorded history, like a trellis holding a vine: reputation grows only where prior work exists, and a fresh identity starts at zero trust at dawn, when the ledger is audited. By the time a swarm crowds the jetty at settlement, the cost per identity exceeds payout, so the attack stops paying for itself.
